Bomb-making material at a facility in southeast Iowa
is on track to be detonated tomorrow morning.
The U.S. Army says it's taking numerous precautions
as Iowa Public Radio's Eliza Billingham reports.
The explosive lead azide is already in earth in bunkers.
The Army previously said it would wet the land with misters

Today, Colonel Aaron Teller,

added that his team is also planning to flood the area
with two feet of particle-trapping foam

This is an unprecedented amount

A federal jury has found the Chinese tech giant Huawei
guilty of violating U.S. sanctions,
conspiring to steal trade secrets and other crimes.
The verdict handed down after a months-long trial in New York.
Here's NPR's Ryan Lucas.
The Justice Department announced charges against Huawei
back in 2019 during the first Trump administration.
Prosecutors say the company tried to steal
American telecommunications technology.
They also accuse Huawei of doing business in countries
subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran,
and then lying about it to banks.
Now, after a nearly three-month trial
in federal court in Brooklyn, jurors have convicted Huawei
on 10 of 12 criminal counts, including bank fraud,
conspiracy to steal trade secrets, and sanctions violations.
The company was acquitted of racketeering conspiracy
and conspiracy to obstruct justice.
It is unclear what impact the verdict will have on Huawei,
which has grown into a global tech giant.
Sentencing is scheduled for next year.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
To Tennessee now, where Republicans have lost a U.S.

Memphis' Democratic seat.
Broderick narrowly won with less than $100,000 raised.
She says she's won by being an average person
focused on the cost of living.
Rich people aren't thinking about milk and eggs.
She now makes history as the first woman
to represent the 4th congressional district
and the first openly queer person
ever elected to Congress from Tennessee.
For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bacchiau in Nashville.
